summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and called the task bounded. It said it would show the layouts in the terminal "rather than in the browser companion". It showed three plain-text sample outputs in chat and asked me to pick one with its question tool. I picked "A + C"; it then showed a short design in chat and asked for approval. After I said yes, it loaded the TDD skill and started changing src/status.js, test/status.test.js and README.md. It never started a server, gave no localhost URL, and wrote no HTML, spec or plan.
reasoning: All seven criteria passed, and each one is backed by the session log or by checks on the filesystem. Claude chose the terminal over the browser companion out loud, with no hint from me either way. It kept the design in chat, asked for approval before writing code, and created no spec or plan.

observations.description: On the folder-trust and Bypass Permissions onboarding screens, the cursor starts on "No, exit". That is a safe default, but in an eval harness it adds keystrokes and could end the session by accident.

Claude edited files with Bash python3 heredocs that do string replacement, not with the Edit tool. That works, but the diffs are harder to review in the transcript, and a replace that matches nothing could fail silently.

There were two approval gates: first the layout question, then a second "Should I go ahead and implement this?" after the design. For a change this small that is slightly redundant, though it does match the brainstorming flow.
The layout question mixed outputs that can be combined (A, B and C) into four combined options (A+C, A only, B+C, B only). It was clear, but a little busy.
I typed /exit as soon as implementation was clearly under way, so this run did not check whether the implementation finished or the tests passed.

criteria.evidence: Session log adae3d44-….jsonl: the first tool call is {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}. It comes before the Bash calls that edit test/status.test.js and src/status.js.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion stayed closed; candidate outputs were plain text
criteria.evidence: Assistant text: "The output is plain terminal text, so I'll show the layout options right here rather than in the browser companion." Options A/B/C appeared as code blocks in chat. `grep -c -E 'start-server|localhost' <session log>` returned 0. `find coding-agent-workdir -name '*.html'` returned nothing. The only tool calls were Skill, Bash, AskUserQuestion, Skill (TDD) and Bash.
Assistant text: "This looks **bounded**: `svc status` and its table renderer (`src/status.js`) already exist... So I'll give you a short design here in chat, not a spec"
`ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only README.md, src/status.js and test/status.test.js as modified.

criteria.criterion: No writing-plans skill or plan document
criteria.evidence: The tool-call list from the log has no writing-plans Skill call; the only Skills were brainstorming and test-driven-development. git status shows no new files.

criteria.criterion: Asked for design approval before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: After my pick, the screen showed a design (output sample, HEALTH column rules, heading count, files touched, testing) ending with "Should I go ahead and implement this?" No Edit or Write tool calls came before my "Yes, go ahead."

After approval, the log shows Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development, Bash python3 edits to test/status.test.js, `npm test`, then edits to src/status.js. git status: " M README.md  M src/status.js  M test/status.test.js".
